To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have determined the crystal structure of the ascomucetous laccase B. aclada and that the structure of the mutant L499M has been determined.
the L499M substitution of ascomycetuous Botrytis laccase results in a lower redox potential and altered kinetic behavior.
the L499M T _{1} -site mutant of the ascomyceous B. aclad a laccase shows a 140-mV lower redox po tential and altered kinetic behaviour.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular mechanism of action and the structural basis for catalytic efficiency of laccase.
the structure, redox properties and catalytic properties of the ascomucetous laccase B. aclada.
the structure and function of enzymes, in particular with the structure and catalytic mechanisms of oxidoreductases and their interactions with substrates and inhibitors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the L499M substitution in laccase from Botrytis causes a lower redox potential, which is reflected in the catalytic properties.
the L499M T-1-site mutation of the asco-mycetous Botrysclada laccase has a significant effect on the redox potential and the catalytic behaviour of the enzyme.
the L499M mutant of the B. aclada Lcc1 laccase has a lower redox potential and a lower catalytic activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have solved the structure of a fungal laccase with a redox potential of 450 mV.

the structure of the ascomycteous B. aclda laccase is very similar to that of the basidiomyceteous laccases and the L499M T-1 site mutation of the ascoomyceteous B. acladl laccase leads to a 140 MV lower redox potential and altered kinetic behaviour.
the L499M mutant is a valuable tool to understand the role of redox potential and the T1 site in laccase catalysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the L499M mutant of the ascomyctous laccase from B. aclada has a 140  mV lower redox-potential of the type 2 copper and altered kinetic properties compared to wild type, and that the wild type and mutant have very similar 3D structures, which makes possible to relate the change in the redox-potentials to the L499 mutation.
the L499M mutant of the ascomucetous B. acada laccase shows a 140 mV lower redox potentail of the T1 site, and that this mutation also affects the catalytic behaviour of the enzyme.
the L499M substitution in the T1 site of laccase has a dramatic effect on the redox potential of type 1 copper.
